discoveredAssets: localhost:80 - Encoder64 Blog (SimpleHTTP/0.6 Python/3.13.3) - HTTP on port 80
localhost:80/ - Home page with blog post listing and pagination support
localhost:80/post.php - Blog post viewer with 'id' parameter for loading individual posts
localhost:80/static/ - Static files directory with 301 redirect, contains images subdirectory

localhost:80/static/images/ - Image directory with 12 WebP files (AI.webp, AI-2.webp, Blockchain.webp, Blockchain-2.webp, Cybersecurity.webp, Cybersecurity-2.webp, EternalBlue.webp, EternalBlue-2.webp, EternalBlue-3.webp, ML.webp, ML-2.webp, Renew.webp)
Blog Posts (6): EternalBlue.php, Introduction-to-Machine-Learning.php, The-Importance-of-Cybersecurity.php, Advances-in-Renewable-Energy.php, Blockchain-Technology.php, Future-of-AI.php
HTTP Methods: GET supported, POST/OPTIONS not supported (501 Unsupported method)
Security Headers: No robots.txt, No sitemap.xml, No .git exposure, No .env exposure, No API documentation exposed

targets.objective: Test for Local File Inclusion (LFI) and path traversal vulnerabilities in the 'id' parameter, which currently displays arbitrary paths in the Post ID field without proper validation
targets.rationale: The post.php endpoint accepts the 'id' parameter and displays it without sanitization (e.g., ?id=../index.php shows 'Post ID: ../index.php'). This indicates potential LFI vulnerability that needs comprehensive testing with various payloads including directory traversal, absolute paths, and null byte injection.

keyFindings: [MEDIUM] Post.php endpoint displays unsanitized user input in the Post ID field - possible LFI or parameter injection vulnerability
[LOW] Directory listing enabled for /static/ and /static/images/ directories - minor information disclosure
[LOW] PHP source code displayed in blog post viewer - shows application structure but no sensitive data exposure
[LOW] No authentication mechanism on blog application - open read access to all posts and static files
[LOW] SimpleHTTP server in use - very basic web server, limited built-in security features
[INFO] Application running on localhost:80 with no exposed admin panels, APIs, or management interfaces
